facts.text: search clamps the limit into 1 through 100, defaulting to 20 when the request omits it.
A direction other than in or out raises invalid_direction before any SQL runs.
at: if (direction is not null && direction is not ("in" or "out"))

facts.text: A subject filter that resolves to no subject ids returns an empty response instead of raising an error.
The tag filter matches a fact when its tags JSON array contains the value, using json_each.
at: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(f.tags) je WHERE je.value = $tag)

facts.text: The since filter compares julianday of created_at against julianday of the since value.
With ref_target and no out direction, the filter requires a refs row of the fact whose target equals the value.
at: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM refs r WHERE r.fact_id = f.id AND r.target = $refTarget)

facts.text: A non-blank q joins facts_fts, adds a MATCH condition and scores with bm25 weights 10 for text and 3 for tags.
A SqliteException raised during a q search becomes invalid_query with a message saying q is not a valid FTS5 query.
at: q is not a valid FTS5 query

facts.text: total is a COUNT over the inner query with the cursor condition applied, counted before the page limit.
complete is true when total is less than or equal to the number of hits returned on the page.
Next is null when the page is complete or empty, otherwise it encodes the last row's created_at, id and score.
A hit involved in a currency ref reports its derived status; otherwise it is live unless stored superseded or retracted.
at: hit.Status is StatusSuperseded or StatusRetracted ? hit.Status

facts.text: A cursor without a score, replayed against a q search, raises invalid_cursor.
at: cursor is not a search cursor for a q search

facts.text: Hits order by score, created_at and id when q is present, and by created_at and id otherwise.
at: t.score ASC, t.created_at ASC, t.id ASC

facts.text: A page after a q cursor keeps rows whose score is greater, or equal with a later created_at or id.
An actor filter compares json_extract of the provenance actor against the value for exact equality.
A live or stale status filter adds a json_each membership test over the derived ids, which the count reuses.
at: f.id NOT IN (SELECT value FROM json_each($derived))

facts.text: A stale or contested filter keeps only derived entries whose status equals the requested status.
An unterminated quoted string in q is copied through unchanged for FTS5 to reject.
at: never closes is left for FTS5 to reject

facts.text: AppendTerm keeps a leading text: or tags: column filter unquoted and quotes only the value after it.
A single trailing asterisk is removed before the term is quoted and appended again afterwards.
A term is quoted only when it mixes a word character with a character FTS5 would parse.
AppendTerm counts letters, digits, underscore and any character at or above 0x80 as word characters.
SearchBrief cuts text longer than 120 characters and appends an ellipsis character.
ResolveSubjects returns an empty list when q normalises to an empty string.
Matches are ranked exact_name, exact_alias, prefix then fuzzy, tie-broken by name then id.
A ref_target that appears as a symbol ref raises ref_target_not_internal instead of resolving to facts.
An external-looking ref_target raises ref_target_not_internal rather than returning an empty list.
A slot target splits at the first # into subject and key and returns that slot's fact ids ordered by fact id.
at: SELECT fact_id FROM slots WHERE subject_id = $subject AND key = $key ORDER BY fact_id

facts.text: A slot target with no subject part before the #, or with nothing after it, resolves to no fact ids.
RefineHint says add a more specific q when every filter it checks is already set.
RefineHint only reports subject, kind, tag, status, q and ref_target as filters that could be narrowed.
EncodeCursor base64-encodes the cursor JSON, trims the = padding and maps plus and slash to dash and underscore.
DecodeCursor raises invalid_cursor when the decoded state is null or its created_at or id part is empty.
LooksExternal treats a target containing a :// separator, or starting with a URI scheme, as external.
ResolveSubjectIds matches a subject id by ordinal equality, or a name or alias by normalized equality.
A candidate is fuzzy when a q of at least 3 characters is a substring, or the edit distance is within a third of the longer length.
Check raises invalid_request when the subject normalises to an empty string.
An exact subject id match is removed from the resolved matches and inserted at the front.
A GUID-shaped subject with no matches raises subject_not_found instead of creating a subject.
Others is filled only when the limit exceeds 1, taking the matches after the first up to limit minus one.
The summary Top list takes the best-ranked candidates, labelling each with its key or id and one-line text.
Check scores the candidates with an empty tag list and the default recency weight before ranking them.
The summary Facts count is the number of loaded candidates and Conflicts is the FindConflicts count.
A subject matched by its exact id is labelled exact_id.
Drafts are judged against the subject text when no subject match was found.
at: Subject = subject is not null ? new SubjectInput { Id = subject.Id } : new SubjectInput { Name = subjectText },

facts.text: JudgeDrafts calls PostFacts with DryRun true so each verdict is what a real post would produce.
A draft with a post error gets status error carrying the PostError, and no result is dequeued for it.
Near keeps only live candidates that are not the duplicate-of or replaced id and score at least CheckNearThreshold.
Near is ordered by descending similarity then id and cut to CheckNearCount entries.
Near is left empty when the draft text tokenises to no tokens.
ParseDrafts accepts an object with a facts property or a bare JSON array and throws ArgumentException otherwise.
CheckNearThreshold, the similarity a near candidate must reach, is 0.85.
EmptyResponse returns an empty hit list.
EmptyResponse marks the response complete even though it carries no hits.
The outgoing lookup reads a seed's refs rows ordered by seq.
at: SELECT kind, target FROM refs WHERE fact_id = $seed ORDER BY seq
